content:
The image shows a corn leaf with the following features:

- Large, heavily blighted leaf with extensive tan/brown necrosis covering most of the leaf surface
- Remnant green tissue in patches, particularly along the midrib area
- Lesions appear to be somewhat rectangular and bounded by leaf veins
- The overall appearance is of a severely diseased leaf progressing toward complete necrosis
- Tan-to-brown coloration with some reddish-brown margins visible
- The lesion pattern shows rectangular spots that coalesce, running along the leaf

The rectangular lesions bounded by leaf veins, tan to brown color with reddish-brown margins, and the severe coalescence forming large necrotic areas strongly match **Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight** (Race O). The pattern of rectangular spots confined by veins, starting light brown with darker margins, is characteristic. This differs from Northern Leaf Blight (which shows cigar/canoe-shaped lesions 1-6 inches long) and Gray Leaf Spot (which has a silvery-gray cast during sporulation and narrower rectangular lesions).
